item.title: Smart lighting technology enables remote color control
item.description: Lighting has evolved from simply illuminating objects to changing their perceived colors. The technology can change the perceived color of specific objects while maintaining natural white illumination in the surrounding space. Visitors will be able to see how the same object appears in different colors at an exhibition to be held at the National Science Museum in Daejeon, South Korea, in November. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Using light to switch molecular states in the smallest of spaces
item.description: What if light could be used not just to observe matter, but to actively reprogram it? Photochromic materials contain molecules that switch between distinct molecular states when exposed to different colors of light. This ability offers exciting possibilities for optical memory and light-controlled electronic devices. However, controlling these molecular changes within extremely small spaces remains challenging because conventional optics cannot focus light to dimensions much smaller than its wavelength. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Israeli writer and filmmaker Etgar Keret, author of "The Seven Good Years", joining us from Tel Aviv. Keret argues that Netanyahu is seeking to remain in power, at any cost, including delegitimizing Arab parties and prolonging conflict. “For him, it could be a never-ending war as long as he's in power. He has no incentive to stop it,” he warns. Keret also calls for Israelis to examine how the war in Gaza was conducted, arguing that “the media as a whole ignored the war.” Fuente: France 24 - English.
